html:
The United Principalities were formed in 1859, when Moldavia and Wallachia each elected the same prince, Alexandru Ioan Cuza, on 5 and 24 January, making them one state that took the name Romania in 1862.

After the Crimean War the great powers let each principality choose its ruler but not unite. Electing the same man got around this. Cuza took the lands of the monasteries, gave land to peasants and founded universities in Iași and Bucharest. He was forced out in 1866, and a German prince, Carol of Hohenzollern, took the throne. Romania won full independence in the war of 1877 and 1878. Its national day celebrates the later union of 1918.
